articles.title: Kilwa grew rich on gold it never mined. Is your product built on someone else's route?
articles.excerpt: In 1944, an Australian soldier named Maurie Isenberg was posted to a radar station on Marchinbar Island, in the Wessel Islands off the far north coast of Australia. In his spare time he went fishing.…
articles.body: In 1944, an Australian soldier named Maurie Isenberg was posted to a radar station on Marchinbar Island, in the Wessel Islands off the far north coast of Australia. In his spare time he went fishing. One day, in the sand just below the high-water mark, he noticed a few small, green, round objects. He picked them up, found a few more nearby, and put them in a tin. The tin stayed in his kit for 35 years. In 1979 he finally had the coins identified. Four were Dutch East India Company coins. The other five were copper coins from the Sultanate of Kilwa, an island city off the coast of what is now southern Tanzania, on the other side of the Indian Ocean. Nobody knows for certain how they got there.

articles.title: Black October: what one week of PHP2Shell, LiteLLM and eMudhra says about who scans your code
articles.excerpt: Between Friday 17 October and Friday 24 October 2026, the PHP interpreter shipped emergency patches for two pre-auth RCEs found with frontier AI models. The fix date was forced forward by a leaked emb…
articles.body: Between Friday 17 October and Friday 24 October 2026, the PHP interpreter shipped emergency patches for two pre-auth RCEs found with frontier AI models. The fix date was forced forward by a leaked embargo. A popular AI proxy shipped a backdoored release to PyPI and Docker Hub, and an Indian certificate authority turned out to have eight intermediate keys that anyone could derive from the public certificates. Node.js pushed ten security fixes on the same day as PHP. Government websites in several European countries went dark on purpose while operators patched. None of these is an exotic attack. Two are old bugs that sat in plain sight until a model went looking. One is a leaked credential that nobody revoked for 136 days.

articles.title: Lalibela's builders carved downward. Some of your deploys are the same
articles.excerpt: High in the Lasta mountains of northern Ethiopia, about 645 kilometres from Addis Ababa, there is a town where the churches are not built. They are carved. Lalibela holds eleven medieval churches cut…
articles.body: High in the Lasta mountains of northern Ethiopia, about 645 kilometres from Addis Ababa, there is a town where the churches are not built. They are carved. Lalibela holds eleven medieval churches cut out of solid volcanic rock. UNESCO lists them as a World Heritage Site, and they were among the very first twelve places inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1978. Their creation is attributed to King Lalibela of the Zagwe dynasty, who ruled in the late twelfth and early thirteenth century. According to UNESCO, he set out to build a "New Jerusalem" after Muslim conquests had halted Christian pilgrimages to the Holy Land. Even the landscape carries the idea: a channel cut through the site is named the Yordannos, the Jordan. Most visitors come to see one church above all.

articles.title: A Major-style live broadcast overlay for CS2 with Game State Integration
articles.excerpt: Watching Major tournaments, the broadcast overlay always caught my eye: every player's health, money and weapons, the killfeed, the bomb timer. I wanted to build something like it for my own matches.…
articles.body: Watching Major tournaments, the broadcast overlay always caught my eye: every player's health, money and weapons, the killfeed, the bomb timer. I wanted to build something like it for my own matches. Getting data out of the game CS2 has a feature called Game State Integration (GSI). You put a file in the game's cfg folder, and during a match the game sends the data you asked for as JSON to the address you gave it. Mine asks for updates every 0.1 seconds, sent to a local server: "Manyaksisko35 GSI v1" { "uri" "http://127.0.0.1:3000" "throttle" "0.1" "data" { "map" "1" "round" "1" "player_state" "1" "allplayers_state" "1" "allplayers_weapons" "1" "allplayers_match_stats" "1" "phase_countdowns" "1" } } A Python server in between The JSON the game sends is big and messy.

articles.title: Lazy Loading in React
articles.excerpt: What Is Lazy Loading? Lazy loading in React is a technique that loads a component only when it is needed instead of loading all components at the beginning of the application. It helps improve applica…
articles.body: What Is Lazy Loading? Lazy loading in React is a technique that loads a component only when it is needed instead of loading all components at the beginning of the application. It helps improve application performance by reducing the amount of JavaScript that needs to be loaded initially. For example, imagine an application with three pages: Home About Dashboard Without lazy loading, the JavaScript for all three pages might be included in the initial bundle, even if the user visits only the Home page. With lazy loading, React can load the Home page first and load the About or Dashboard page when the user navigates to it. Why Do We Use Lazy Loading? Lazy loading offers several benefits: Improves initial loading speed: The browser downloads less JavaScript when the application first opens.

articles.title: The Minimum Friction of Truth: An Open Letter to Harun on Building a Biophysical Trust Kernel and Why His Thesis Changes Everything
articles.excerpt: An Open Letter to Harun Harun, I almost never write articles addressed directly to a single developer. In our industry, technical writing is usually sanitized, polished for corporate PR, or wrapped in…
articles.body: An Open Letter to Harun Harun, I almost never write articles addressed directly to a single developer. In our industry, technical writing is usually sanitized, polished for corporate PR, or wrapped in algorithmic jargon to attract venture capital. But while reading through your work on bio-os and the challenges you tackled during your development sprints, I encountered two sentences you wrote that stopped me in my tracks: "If an AI hallucinates while writing web code, your app crashes. If an AI hallucinates while writing DNA sequences or quantum algorithms, the consequences are catastrophic." Those two sentences are not merely clever rhetoric. They are the most succinct, mathematically accurate definition of the fundamental epistemic problem facing modern artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Rubin telescope should find more of Earth's mysterious 'mini-moons' — including some we can study up close
articles.excerpt: Earth’s tiny, temporary moons could become some of the easiest asteroid targets for future missions. And we'll likely find more of them soon, thanks to the Rubin telescope.
articles.body: Earth almost always has more than one moon. The others are just very small, and they never stay long — but they could provide accessible and unique insights into the solar system. Temporary satellites, or mini-moons , are small asteroids that wander into Earth’s neighborhood and get captured briefly by our planet’s gravity. A typical one stays about nine months and circles Earth roughly three times before escaping back into orbit around the sun , Grigori Fedorets of Finland's University of Helsinki said in a presentation at the Europlanet Science Congress (EPSC) 2026 in The Hague in September. Fedorets' modeling suggests that the largest mini-moon around Earth at any given moment is typically only about 75 centimeters (30 inches) across.

articles.title: October full 'Hunter's Moon' dazzles in spectacular photos from around the world
articles.excerpt: Feast your eyes on the best photos of October's full 'Hunter's Moon'.
articles.body: The full "Hunter's Moon" wowed stargazers with a breathtaking display of natural light when it rose to dominate the autumn sky overnight on Oct. 25-26. Here are our favorite photos captured from around the world. October's full moon is often known as the Hunter's Moon because it traditionally rose around the time that hunters would take to the newly harvested fields to catch animals to prepare as food for the coming winter. Well, in 2026 the Hunter's Moon certainly succeeded in captivating the imagination and attention of photographers, who snapped the lunar disk alongside magnificent natural vistas, glowing cityscapes and ancient wonders. Read on to enjoy the most spectacular images of the Hunter's Moon.
